newsitem.title: FRANCE: Slovak PM warns NATO of danger of polarisation.
newsitem.headline: Slovak PM warns NATO of danger of polarisation.

text.p: Slovak Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar warned on Thursday that Western failure to reach security agreements with Russia could push Moscow into new alliances with China and the Arab world, creating an undesirable polarisation.
"Russia cannot remain isolated because it will start looking for natural partners," Meciar told the Western European Union's (WEU) parliamentary assembly.

"If Russia feels threatened or isolated, there is a great probability it will intensify its relations with China and the Arab countries and it is in no one's interest to have such a polarisation of forces," he said.

Saying his country "did not want to get crushed again between Germany and Russia", Meciar called for an acceleration of talks between the West and Russia on security issues parallel to the extension of NATO to former Warsaw Pact states.

"We are committed to Slovakia's membership in NATO but believe the enlargement process should be well thought-out and not lead to new tensions and misunderstandings. If ties between Russia and the U.S. are positive, the world will be a safer place to live for everyone.
"(However) in my talks with Russian officials, they ask that if NATO is not directed against Russia, why does it not yet have treaties with Moscow?" he said.

There was a danger that some members of the Russian military establishment could feel cheated or threatened by the enlargement process, he said in separate statements, including a prepared speech and a news conference.
"Russia cannot be left out because although it is weaker than the former Soviet Union...it has a potential and the ambition to conduct a superpower policy," he said.
Meciar said Russia had already initiated new contacts with Arab states and was cooperating with Iran over a possible nuclear power plant.

"Intensive negotiations have also started taking place between Russian and Chinese representatives concerning possible cooperation and both take a critical view of some of the policies of the United States," he said.

Polish President Aleksander Kwasniewski told the same forum on Wednesday he believed Russian fears about the admission of its former East European satellites into NATO would fade like the fears which initially surrounded German unification.
Slovakia, like Poland, wants to join the 10-nation WEU as well as NATO.

At French instigation, the 1991 Maastricht Treaty designated the WEU the future defence arm of the European Union, but Britain has since opposed bringing the defence grouping under the authority of the EU's summit of heads of state and government.
Meciar, like Kwasniewski, was careful not to offend any side in a tug-of-war between the United States and France over the existence of a European pillar within NATO.
